text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong says Singaporeans voting in the January 2 election will see effects of their vote immediately.
- People's Action Party returns to power by winning 47 out of 83 seats without any contest.
- Two more former directors of Amcol Holdings charged with insider trading by Commercial Affairs Department.
- Retailer CK Tang reports smaller Singapore $7.2 million interim group net loss and achieves operating profit of $955,000.
- Developers of proposed Singapore Exchange Centre close to reaching settlement with Land Office on differential premium.
- Commercial Affairs Department continues probe into service apartments pioneer Scotts Holdings.
- Two former Citibank executives set up fund management company to manage global equity portfolios for institutional and high net worth clients.
- Malaysian infrastructure developer YTL Corp Bhd proposes a one-for-two bonus issue, a special issue and a bond issue.
- Inchcape Timuran Bhd gets takeover notice from Arus Murni Sdn Bhd to acquire the remainng 51 percent equity in ITB.
- Bousteadco Singapore reports 42.4 percent decline in interim net profit to Singapore $534,000 for half year ended September 30.
